items.title: Topic Fourteen, Sub-Part 6: What Makes Speech Genuinely Good

items.zh: 賢聖常說最善語；愛非不愛語第二；諦非不諦語第三；法非非法語第四。
items.en: The noble ones always speak the most excellent speech; pleasing, not displeasing, second; true, not false, third; in accord with the Dharma, not against it, fourth.

items.zh: 今此頌中，言善語者，所謂善說、善言、善論。當知善說有三種相。所謂悅意、無染、唯善。由第一語，令他慶悅。由第二語，令自尸羅終無穿缺。由第三語，能令他人出不善處，安住善處，因此引攝利益安樂。或有愛語，非諦、非法。謂如有一，以美妙言，稱讚他人非真實德。或有諦語，非愛、非法。謂如有一，以染污心，發麁惡言，訶責他人真實過惡。或有法語，亦愛亦諦。謂如有一，善知稱讚及與訶責。知可稱讚、可訶責已，然不稱讚，亦不訶責，唯善方便為說正法，能令彼人出不善處安住善處。復次，今當略辨上所說義。謂薄伽梵此中略示，所有善語，若標、若釋。當知是名此中略義。
items.en: In this verse, 'excellent speech' means good saying, good words and good discourse. Good saying should be understood to have three marks: it is pleasing, it is untainted, and it is purely wholesome. By the first kind of speech one gladdens others. By the second, one's own precepts are never breached. By the third, one is able to lead others out of unwholesome conditions and establish them in wholesome conditions, and thereby bring about benefit and happiness. There is pleasing speech that is neither true nor in accord with the Dharma: someone, with fine words, praises in others virtues they do not really have. There is true speech that is neither pleasing nor in accord with the Dharma: someone, with a defiled mind, utters harsh words rebuking others for faults they really have. There is speech in accord with the Dharma that is both pleasing and true: someone knows well how to praise and how to rebuke; having recognised what deserves praise and what deserves rebuke, they neither praise nor rebuke, but simply, with skilful means, teach the true Dharma, which is able to lead that person out of unwholesome conditions and establish them in wholesome conditions. Further, the meaning of what was said above will now be briefly set out. In this verse the Blessed One briefly shows all excellent speech, both by naming it and by explaining it. It should be understood that this is the summary meaning here.

items.title: Sub-Part 7: The Fruit of Genuine Practice, for Renunciant and Householder Alike

items.zh: 信、慚、戒、施、法、善人所稱讚；是名趣天道，能往天世間。
items.en: Faith, a sense of shame, precepts, generosity, and the Dharma — this is what the good praise, this is called the path to the heavens, and by this one is able to go to the heavenly worlds.

items.zh: 此頌所明，謂如有一，於佛所證法毘奈耶，獲得正信。恥在居家。受持淨戒。趣得衣服、飲食、臥具，便生喜足；減除器物，儉約資緣。凡所獲得如法利養，終無私隱，必與智人同梵行者而共受用。所有正法初中後善，稱揚梵行，所謂契經乃至論議，皆能受持、研尋、究達，傳授他人，廣為開闡。彼既成就是諸善法，當知必獲三種勝利。一者、諸佛諸佛弟子真實善人之所稱讚。二者、若彼尸羅財施之所攝引福德資糧、法施攝引智慧資糧善圓滿者，便得趣入證解脫處，清淨諸天眾同分中。三者、若彼二種資糧猶未圓滿，便能令彼速得圓滿。身壞已後定生善趣，多往天上樂世界中。復有差別。謂如有一，於佛所證法毘奈耶獲得正信；信惡尸羅當墮惡趣，信慳貪者得貧窮報。如是信已，於現法中惡戒、慳貪深生羞恥。以羞恥故，棄惡尸羅，受清淨戒；棄捨慳貪，以無垢心安處居家，廣說乃至善行布施。由此因緣，於現法中聖賢所讚；身壞已後，乃至當生善趣天上樂世界中。復次，今當略辨上所說義。謂薄伽梵此中略示，在家、出家二種正行，及正行果所有勝利。當知是名此中略義。
items.en: This verse explains the following. Someone gains right faith in the Dharma and Vinaya realised by the Buddha. They feel shame at remaining in household life. They take up and keep the pure precepts. Whatever clothing, food and drink, and bedding they come by, they are content with; they reduce their belongings and are frugal in their requisites. Whatever gains they obtain in accordance with the Dharma, they never keep hidden for themselves, but always share them with wise companions in the holy life. The true Dharma, good in the beginning, middle and end, which extols the holy life, namely the discourses and so on up to the treatises, they are all able to take up and keep, investigate, penetrate thoroughly, pass on to others and expound widely. Having accomplished these wholesome qualities, they should be understood to gain without fail three benefits. First, they are praised by the buddhas, the buddhas' disciples and truly good people. Second, if their store of merit, drawn in by precepts and the giving of material things, and their store of wisdom, drawn in by the giving of the Dharma, are well fulfilled, they are able to enter the place where liberation is realised, among the company of the pure gods. Third, if those two stores are not yet fulfilled, these qualities enable them to fulfil them quickly. After the breaking up of the body they are certain to be reborn in a good destiny, mostly going to the happy worlds of the heavens. There is a further distinction. Someone gains right faith in the Dharma and Vinaya realised by the Buddha; they believe that those of bad conduct will fall into the bad destinies, and that the miserly receive poverty as their result. Having this faith, they feel deep shame here and now at bad conduct and at miserliness. Because of this shame, they abandon bad conduct and take up the pure precepts; they abandon miserliness and, with a mind free of stain, settle in household life, and so on at length, up to practising generosity well. For this reason they are praised here and now by the noble and the worthy, and after the breaking up of the body they will be reborn, and so on, in the happy worlds of the heavens, a good destiny. Further, the meaning of what was said above will now be briefly set out. In this verse the Blessed One briefly shows the two kinds of right practice, of householders and of those gone forth, and all the benefits that are the fruit of right practice. It should be understood that this is the summary meaning here.

items.title: Sub-Part 8: How Extensive Learning Leads All the Way to Nirvāṇa

items.zh: 多聞能知法；多聞能遠惡；多聞捨無義；多聞得涅槃。
items.en: Through extensive learning one knows the teaching; through extensive learning one keeps far from evil; through extensive learning one relinquishes what is meaningless; through extensive learning one attains nirvāṇa.

items.zh: 此頌所明，謂如有一，於依先時正所應作施論、戒論、生天之論，無倒教法恭敬聽聞；聞已遂能了知其義。謂現法中種種惡行，及當惡趣苦無義因諸惡行所，應速遠離；及往善趣，捨生惡趣苦無義因。彼由了知如是法義，法隨法行，能遠苦因、能引樂因；由此因緣，得樂捨苦。若於增上四聖諦等相應教法恭敬聽聞，聞已遂能了知其義。謂一切有生死大苦寂靜涅槃。彼由了知如是法義，若根已熟，資糧已滿，便能獲得如是義識。心清淨故，纔聞法已，於諸聖諦未現觀者，能入現觀；已現觀者，便得漏盡。若根未熟，資糧未滿，即由如是遠離諸惡，依增上戒起增上心，依增上心發增上慧，由此能捨一切苦本煩惱無義，證得涅槃。復次，今當略辨上所說義。謂薄伽梵此中略示，先聞正法，如理思惟；先如理思，法隨法行；法隨法行為先因故，得勝利果。當知是名此中略義。
items.en: This verse explains the following. Someone respectfully listens to the unerring teaching that should properly come first, namely talk on giving, talk on precepts and talk on rebirth in heaven, and having heard it, comes to understand its meaning: that the various kinds of bad conduct here and now, which are the meaningless causes of suffering in the bad destinies to come, should quickly be abandoned; and that one should go to the good destinies and give up the meaningless causes of the suffering of rebirth in the bad destinies. Having understood the meaning of such teachings, they practise the Dharma in accordance with the Dharma, so that they can keep far from the causes of suffering and bring about the causes of happiness; for this reason they gain happiness and leave suffering behind. Again, they respectfully listen to the teachings connected with higher matters, such as the four noble truths, and having heard them, come to understand their meaning: that all existence is the great suffering of birth-and-death, and that nirvana is peace. Having understood the meaning of such teachings, if their faculties are already ripe and their stores already full, they are able to gain consciousness of this meaning. Because their mind is pure, as soon as they hear the Dharma, if they have not yet directly realised the noble truths they are able to enter direct realisation; if they have already directly realised them, they attain the exhaustion of the outflows. If their faculties are not yet ripe and their stores not yet full, then through keeping far from all evils in this way, relying on higher morality they give rise to higher mind, and relying on higher mind they develop higher wisdom; by this they are able to relinquish the afflictions, the root of all suffering and meaningless, and realise nirvana. Further, the meaning of what was said above will now be briefly set out. In this verse the Blessed One briefly shows this: first one hears the true Dharma and then reflects on it properly; first one reflects properly and then practises the Dharma in accordance with the Dharma; and with practising the Dharma in accordance with the Dharma as the prior cause, one obtains the fruit of benefit. It should be understood that this is the summary meaning here.

blocks.text: Fascicle 19 is the last of the Stage of Reflection. It continues the essential-body verses: short, memorable verses on everyday practice, each with an explanation. Ru-Yi translates the verses, but **the prose explanations are missing from Ru-Yi's translation**; the English column gives our own translation, marked as ours, and the commentary also summarises them.
"The noble ones always speak the most excellent speech; pleasing, not displeasing, second; true, not false, third; in accord with the Dharma, fourth."

The prose (our translation, 0381b26–c11): good speech is **pleasing** (it gladdens the listener), **unstained** (it keeps one's own precepts whole), and **only good** (it brings the listener from the unwholesome to the wholesome). Some speech is pleasing but neither true nor Dharma: flattering praise of qualities someone lacks. Some is true but neither pleasing nor Dharma: harsh, angry criticism of real faults. Dharma speech is both pleasing and true: knowing what deserves praise and blame, one neither praises nor blames, but simply teaches the Dharma in a way that leads the other to the good.
Master Cháng Bǎi: a parent who scolds a child loudly, to turn them from bad to good, is speaking truly, and perhaps even in accord with Dharma.

"Faith, a sense of shame, precepts, generosity, and the Dharma: this is what the good praise, the path to the heavens." The prose (our translation): someone gains faith, feels ashamed of household entanglement, keeps pure precepts, is content with simple requisites, shares what they receive, and learns and teaches the Dharma. They gain three benefits: praise from the good; entry, if their merit and wisdom are complete, among the pure gods; and, if not yet complete, their swift completion and rebirth in heaven. A householder who believes that bad conduct leads to bad destinies and stinginess to poverty, and changes accordingly, gains the same. Master Cháng Bǎi: the "good" who praise are the noble ones.

"Through extensive learning one knows the teaching, keeps far from evil, relinquishes what is meaningless, attains nirvāṇa." The prose (our translation): hearing first the teachings on giving, precepts, and heaven, one learns what to avoid and what to do; hearing the teachings on the four truths, one with ripe faculties may realise the truths on hearing; one whose faculties are not yet ripe practises the three trainings in order.
Master Cháng Bǎi: learning that stays as knowledge, never practised in body, speech, and mind, does not count as "extensive learning".

quiz.q: According to the sixth verse of discourse, what kinds of speech do the noble ones speak?
options: the most excellent speech; pleasing, not displeasing, second; true, not false, third; in accord with the Dharma, not against it, fourth
frivolous, false, divisive, and harsh speech
quiz.why: The verse: the noble ones always speak the most excellent speech; pleasing, not displeasing, is second; true, not false, third; in accord with the Dharma, not against it, fourth. Venerable Miào Jìng: the second line is pleasing speech, the third true speech, the fourth Dharma speech.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish 賢 (worthy) from 聖 (noble)?
options: the worthy study the noble path but have not realised it, having reached the stage of application; the noble have realised it
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the worthy are studying the noble path but have not yet realised it, having reached the stage of application; the noble have already realised it. He glosses 嘗 as "always."

quiz.q: A mother scolds her child loudly and fiercely. Does Master Cháng Bǎi count this as good speech?
options: though fierce, the motive is to turn the child towards good — it is true speech, and may also be pleasing and Dharma speech
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: though fierce and loud, the inner motive is to have the child turn from bad to good, so this is true speech, and possibly pleasing or Dharma speech too. Venerable Miào Jìng: rebuking someone's real faults out of anger is what is "true but neither pleasing nor in accord with the Dharma."

quiz.q: Who are the "true good people" who praise these five, according to the two masters?
options: noble ones with uncontaminated wisdom; ordinary people are sometimes good and sometimes not, so they are not true good people
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: true good people are noble ones who have realised uncontaminated wisdom; ordinary good people are not truly good, since they are sometimes good and sometimes not. Venerable Miào Jìng: those who have attained the noble path are true good people — without evil intent, compassionate, not ordinary beings.

quiz.q: What four benefits of extensive learning does the eighth verse name?
options: knowing the teaching, keeping far from evil, relinquishing what is meaningless, attaining nirvāṇa
quiz.why: "Through extensive learning one knows the teaching; keeps far from evil; relinquishes what is meaningless; attains nirvāṇa." Venerable Miào Jìng: these four lines appear in the *Mahāvibhāṣā* and in *The Way to Buddhahood*, with a few words changed.

quiz.q: What, per Master Cháng Bǎi, truly counts as "extensive learning"?
options: it must be practised in one's body, speech, and mind; merely accumulating knowledge is not extensive learning
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: if one hears a great deal but only learns it as knowledge, without putting it into practice in body, speech, and mind, that does not count as extensive learning — it is merely accumulated knowledge.

quiz.q: How do the two masters explain "what is meaningless" in "relinquishes what is meaningless"?
options: Cháng Bǎi: 義 here means benefit, so 無義 is what is unprofitable; Miào Jìng: it includes non-Buddhist austerities and also the afflictions
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 義 has two readings — meaning and benefit; here the sense of benefit is taken. Venerable Miào Jìng: "the meaningless" includes non-Buddhist austerities, which are causes of the meaningless, and also the afflictions.
